purpose: Unresolved implementation questions and optional follow-up research. These entries are leads, not supporting evidence or settled product requirements.

leads.topic: A tested Jupyter execution and environment matrix
leads.why_it_matters: JupyterLab/Server, nbformat, nbclient, ipykernel, Python, DuckDB Python and DuckDB CLI versions must work together in both interactive and fresh-kernel replay. Docs/API examples do not qualify an actual combination.
leads.next_step: Pick OS/Python targets, pin exact versions and hashes in a project lock/build, then test notebook open, interactive execution, nbclient replay, error capture, interrupt, cancellation and reopen from a clean machine.
leads.bounded_fallback: Support one explicitly tested Python environment and static viewing when it is unavailable; do not imply arbitrary kernel support.

leads.topic: Untrusted notebook execution confinement across platforms
leads.state: design proposed; not implemented or adversarially tested
leads.why_it_matters: Jupyter Server access permits arbitrary code. A rootless OCI worker, read-only inputs, disabled network, resource limits and termination policy need platform-specific validation. Container isolation is defense-in-depth and can disrupt ordinary interactive file access.
leads.next_step: Prototype Linux rootless worker first; threat-model mounts, runtime sockets, symlinks/path traversal, extension installation, process descendants, disk exhaustion, output validation and cancellation. Evaluate macOS/Windows runtime/mount behavior separately.
leads.bounded_fallback: Disable clean replay if a supported confined runtime is absent; if offering trusted local execution, label its access and guarantees explicitly.

leads.topic: Full content identity cost for external large datasets
leads.why_it_matters: A full SHA-256 is stronger than path/size/mtime but can reread multi-gigabyte sources and delay run startup; weak metadata cannot verify unchanged bytes.
leads.next_step: Measure streaming digest throughput and cancellation on local/removable/network storage; consider cached digest keyed by stable file identity only as an optimization, then revalidate before a run.
leads.bounded_fallback: Label inputs weak/unverified until the content hash is complete; prohibit a verified-current claim when content identity is unknown.

leads.topic: Atomic commit and locking on ordinary folders and network filesystems
leads.state: recovery protocol proposed; filesystem behavior unverified
leads.why_it_matters: Rename durability, lock semantics and concurrent writers vary across platforms, sync folders and network mounts. A portable project exchange promise needs explicit filesystem support boundaries.
leads.next_step: Fault-inject save interruption around staging, fsync, rename and pointer update; test writer races and recovery on supported filesystems and reject unvalidated network write targets.
leads.bounded_fallback: Support read-only inspection on unverified mounts and create conflict copies on stale manifest hashes.

leads.topic: 5 GB input on an 8-core/16 GB workstation
leads.state: target only; no performance check executed
leads.why_it_matters: Lazy scans and out-of-core query execution do not make every join, sort, pivot, aggregation or Python conversion fit memory. Temp disk and OS cache behavior matter.
leads.next_step: Run reproducible projection/filter, bounded preview, result export and blocking-operator benchmarks over generated data while measuring peak RSS, temp usage and elapsed time; publish workload-specific results.
leads.bounded_fallback: Disable or require explicit budgets for operations known to materialize large results; never promise that 5 GB always fits.

leads.topic: Polars lazy/streaming transforms with DuckDB SQL kept separate
leads.why_it_matters: Could be useful if the analysts want a Python dataframe API or a tested scan mode DuckDB does not meet for their actual transforms, but a second engine complicates SQL parity, cache keys, order and output comparison.
leads.next_step: Benchmark the same declared fixture/workloads and compare conversion behavior, lazy boundaries, spill behavior, schema evolution, Python materialization and how the SQL colleague can reproduce outputs.
leads.bounded_fallback: Do not introduce a second engine without a named workload demonstrating a benefit.

leads.why_it_matters: A visual dependency view from declared datasets and transforms to output artifacts can make stale results explainable and surface changed fields or reject counts. Arbitrary notebook dependencies remain unknowable in general.
leads.next_step: Prototype lineage only for declared transform nodes first; show source/contract/code hash diffs and list notebook outputs as unverified unless their inputs are declared.
leads.bounded_fallback: Use conservative whole-notebook invalidation when dependency edges cannot be proven.

leads.topic: Notebook document interchange versus execution specification
leads.state: basic nbformat docs reviewed; cross-implementation portability untested
leads.why_it_matters: Standard `.ipynb` makes projects inspectable and exchangeable, but optional metadata and output attachments do not define a portable kernel, execution environment or provenance event model.
leads.next_step: Test a minimal notebook saved/opened by two current Jupyter front ends and a non-Jupyter viewer; check cell IDs, MIME outputs, widgets and unknown metadata retention against chosen nbformat pins.
leads.bounded_fallback: Use `.ipynb` for document interchange and keep run manifests as a separate versioned project record.
